system: Animation tuning table and critically damped spring
what: One data object holds every animation knob: gait (duty, pelvis drop, lift, cadence bounds), spring stiffnesses, carry / ADS / sprint hold poses per hold style (rifle, smg, scatter; each gun picks one through its GUN_KIT hold), reload choreography keys, and action poses (flinch, death, draw, bayonet charge, throw, shield, katana). An analytic critically damped spring smooths most blended values and stays stable at any frame time (velocity and throw wind-up use their own exponential smoothing, lines 279 and 370). Module-level scratch vectors, quaternions and arrays are reused every frame so the layer itself allocates no math objects.

v2_note: Keep it as plain data (a JSON or TS const the Anim Lab can export into). springStep is small, allocation-free and frame-rate independent: port it as is. Keep the scratch objects module-level in v2 too; they back the header's zero-allocation claim (230), which AUDIT_BUGS_PERF.md P1 contradicts for the layer as a whole (GA15), so v2 must verify it with a profiler. ANIM.aim.carry/ads are dead data (see GA16); only ANIM.aim.adsK is read. No LOOP_V2 section changes it.
reason: Client-side cosmetic tuning data plus a stable smoothing helper, worth keeping in shape.

system: Per-soldier animation state setup and rig fix-ups
what: Builds the soldier's animation state (springs, two foot records, limb lengths, saved hand rotations, death record) on its first anim tick, or straight away when a bot spawns so a kill before its first animated frame still falls. It measures where the fist sits beyond the wrist (skipping held sword, axe and shield) and re-hangs the boot parts under a new ankle pivot because the rig has no ankle joint. Re-init reuses an existing pivot.

what: Derives each soldier's velocity from its position change (teleports re-plant), computes walk/run/sprint weights, turns the hips toward movement within a twist budget (backpedal keeps hips to the aim, no flip), and sizes stride and cadence from the legs' real reach at the current crouch height.

reason: Cosmetic locomotion driven purely by replicated position; the sim never reads it.

what: Each foot is planted in the world, swinging along an arc to the next foothold, or doing a timed step. Swings move relative to the moving stance spot so a foot never trails. Catch-up steps fire when a planted foot is left out of reach, and idle re-steps fire when standing turns stray a foot (turn in place). While the soldier is airborne (st.grounded false) both feet are tucked 0.18 m above the root, pitched 0.25 rad, and re-planted on landing.

The airborne tuck needs a replicated grounded flag per soldier from the sim's vertical state. ANIMATION_PLAN.md §8 item 5 plans to reuse it for the Juggernaut walker.
reason: Cosmetic foot placement; port its logic and add terrain sampling.

system: Per-frame animation driver and its input contract
what: Every frame, the player and every alive bot fill one shared state struct (aim yaw, clock, kick, reload dip, reload progress, throw charge, bayonet lean, grounded, ADS, draw timer) and call updateSoldierAnim. Bots pass no kick, reload, throw or draw. Aim pitch travels outside the struct: pitchWeapon writes the gun's rotation.x, and updateSoldierAnim spots a fresh value by comparing it with the value it stored after last frame's posing, then feeds it into the carry and ADS pitch. Nothing culls or simplifies animation for distant or off-screen soldiers.
where: shamble-game.js:204 _animSt; 271 updateSoldierAnim(g, st, dt); player caller 2782; bot caller 2936; aim-pitch side channel: read 369 (A.aimPitch when wp.rotation.x !== A.wrx), used 373-375, stored back 417, written by pitchWeapon 1428-1432 (player call 2711, bot calls 2903/2921/2925; owned by GC6); ANIM v2 header comment 224-230
evidence: ANIMATION_PLAN.md §6: CPU per soldier per frame ~51 µs (target < 60 µs); AUDIT_BUGS_PERF.md runtime profile: soldier anim 0.18 ms for 7; P1: updateSoldierAnim 17 % of ~8 MB/s garbage plus Quaternion.invert (anim) 5 %; CS11: residual ~4.9 MB/s, optional updateSoldierAnim split expected -1.5 MB/s, held; STATUS.md risk 2: DM_Tri 48 soldiers 7.2-8.2 MB per game second
v2_note: The st struct plus aim pitch is the list of cosmetic fields a v2 snapshot or event stream must carry per soldier (aim yaw and pitch, ADS, reload progress, throw charge, draw, grounded, ability state); make aim pitch an explicit field, not a side channel through the gun's rotation. The header claims zero per-frame allocation, but the audit measured it as a top allocator: v2 must verify this with a profiler. At 48+ soldiers, plan distance or visibility LOD and update-rate cuts: by arithmetic from the 51 µs figure, 48 soldiers is about 2.4 ms per frame. The 2-bone/ankle work could move to a worker or GPU skinning.
reason: Client-side driver; keep the contract as the replicated cosmetic state, add LOD for 48+ soldiers.
